10-frame cross-dissolve (f264-f274) from the city wall to the tent; protagonist and tent interior overlap in f267-f270.
Hard cut inside the tent from a medium two-shot to a close-up of the captain with the protagonist's head in the foreground; new camera, same set.
Really a cross-dissolve (f540-f548) from the tent window view to a dark gatehouse with lanterns and a seated guard; similar framing made the detector call it in-place.
7-frame cross-dissolve from the lantern-lit gatehouse to the moonlit hillside; the moon fades in over the lanterns (f575).
Hard cut from the protagonist on the moonlit hill to a ground-level view of the bomb rolling toward the camp; same staging as the hook shot.
Hard cut from the grinning soldier holding the bomb to a wide low-angle camp shot of a soldier raising a sword.

No second scene appears in f1317-f1324: same shot, lightning arcs grow around the bomb and the cone-hat soldier changes pose; FX flashes fooled the detector.
f1336-f1345: lightning fades while the camera pans onto the bomb, which then splits open (f1356-f1376); one continuous 3D take, no dissolve.

beats.name: hook
beats.said: He sends a bomb rolling toward the enemy camp but rigs it so it will not explode.
beats.shown: Protagonist rolls a small bomb by a lantern post, hard cut to a ground-level view behind a giant bomb rolling toward a moonlit bonfire camp; captions word by word.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: Ten thousand samurai besiege his city and will strike at dawn; he presents his bomb to the captain.
beats.shown: Camera lifts into an aerial fly-over of a field of tents and the town, protagonist on the city wall holding the bomb, dissolve into the captain's tent with a smug protagonist.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Captain scorns a bomb that never explodes; the inventor sneaks out and rolls it into camp.
beats.shown: Tent close-ups: captain shocked then angry with a vein mark, protagonist sweating; captain asleep; dissolves via a gatehouse to the moonlit hill; bomb rolls to the fire, guards dive away.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: No blast; soldiers shake the dud, hope for treasure, snap swords on it, and bet on cracking it.
beats.shown: Quiet beat, then a soldier picks up and shakes the bomb; star-eyed greed grin; sword strike with sparks; crowd around a black drum with a tray of gold coins and a tally board.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Names the weapon; inside is a wooden tube wound with fuse that burns slowly, not in seconds.
beats.shown: Torch-lit soldiers, lightning arcs on the bomb, then the shell splits open into a 3D cutaway: a giant wooden spool with a glowing creeping fuse, sparks, repeated close-ups.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: As the biggest soldier raises a hammer to smash it, the fuse finally hits the gunpowder.
beats.shown: Dawn camp: antlered samurai with red glowing eyes lifts a mallet, sweat drop; red cracks spread from the bomb; fireball fills the frame and whites out.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Final words play over the blast; the clip ends right on the explosion, no outro.
beats.shown: Two deadpan characters on the city wall watch a mushroom cloud, impact ticks around them; video cuts off on the blast with no outro.

hook.first_frame: Night, long shot: teal-robed protagonist leans forward on a dirt road beside a glowing paper-lantern post, a small black bomb in his swung-back hand; caption 'He' low-centre.
hook.first_3s: 0-0.83 s he rolls the bomb (head turns in 3D); hard cut at 0.83 s to a ground-level view behind a giant bomb rolling toward a moonlit bonfire camp while the camera creeps in; captions swap every 0.2-0.4 s.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title asks why samurai feared a named weapon; the first line instead opens on a paradox (a bomb rolled in but rigged not to explode) and the weapon's name only comes at about 42 s.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: A long fuse coiled around a wooden core inside a sealed shell burns slowly, so a seeming dud can explode long after it lands.
story.protagonist: Inventor-soldier in a teal robe who built the slow-fuse bomb
story.authority_or_antagonist: His captain, then the besieging samurai army and their commander
story.explainer_turn: 'what's in there' at 41.4 s; the weapon is named at 42.5 s

tone.humour: Light slapstick and irony: guards leap for cover from a dud, then treat it like treasure and bet on it; cartoon symbols (sweat drop, anger vein, star eyes) add gags.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Dramatic irony: viewers know the fuse is burning while everyone calls it a dud; deadpan half-lidded faces, and two flat-faced survivors watch a mushroom cloud.
tone.dialogue_style: Third-person narration; only two quoted lines, both the captain's; the speaking mouth flaps on those lines while other characters stay mute (estimate).

generation_evidence.observation: Bomb opens in a clean exploded view: shell halves, star shards and discs fly apart on smooth paths while the camera pans to the spool; geometry stays consistent frame to frame.
One continuous aerial fly-over with correct parallax over trees, houses and thousands of tiny tents and torches; nothing morphs between frames.
Protagonist keeps identical outline, pinstripe robe, hair band and gold pin for 1.7 s while the arm lifts the bomb in front of the moon; stone texture stays crisp.
Captain's face swaps discrete eye sets and mouth shapes under a steady ink outline while hat, body and set stay rock solid; reads as keyframed swaps.
Hook shot and the 20 s shot share the same camp staging (bench with three seated soldiers, fire, moon, banners) from different cameras: re-used assets.
Thumbnail-frame detail: tally marks on the board, studded drum, specular gold coins and square-pixel stubble stay crisp with no warping.
